claim: PDK1 expression is elevated in Tfh cells compared with naïve CD4+ T or Th1 cells on day 8 post-LCMV Armstrong infection
source: We infected wild-type C57BL/6J mice with LCMV Armstrong strain and observed elevated expression level of PDK1 in Tfh cells compared with naïve CD4+ T or Th1 cells on day 8 post-infection (8 dpi), which suggested potential roles of PDK1 in Tfh cells (Figure 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1A and described in the text.

claim: PDK1 deficiency in T cells causes a 26.5-fold decrease in Tfh cell generation in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared to WT mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: On 8 dpi, generations of Tfh cells (26.5-fold) and Th1 cells (2.6-fold) were substantially decreased in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice (Figure 1C,D), indicating PDK1 has a more crucial role for Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis and quantification data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: PDK1 deficiency in T cells causes a 2.6-fold decrease in Th1 cell generation in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared to WT mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: On 8 dpi, generations of Tfh cells (26.5-fold) and Th1 cells (2.6-fold) were substantially decreased in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice (Figure 1C,D), indicating PDK1 has a more crucial role for Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis and quantification data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: PDK1 has a more crucial role for Tfh cell differentiation than for Th1 cell differentiation
source: On 8 dpi, generations of Tfh cells (26.5-fold) and Th1 cells (2.6-fold) were substantially decreased in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice (Figure 1C,D), indicating PDK1 has a more crucial role for Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the differential magnitude of reduction in Tfh cells (26.5-fold) versus Th1 cells (2.6-fold) in PDK1-deficient mice.

claim: GC Tfh cells are significantly reduced in PDK1-deficient mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Moreover, GC Tfh cells were also significantly reduced in PDK1-deficient mice (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1C,D.

claim: The expression levels of PD-1, ICOS, and Bcl-6 are much lower in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells than in WT Tfh cells
source: Consistently, the expression levels of PD-1, ICOS, and Bcl-6 were much lower in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells than those of WT cells (Figure 1E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis shown in Figure 1E,F.

claim: PDK1 is essential for Tfh cell differentiation during viral infection
source: Collectively, these data indicated that PDK1 is essential for Tfh cell differentiation during viral infection.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental observations including reduced Tfh cells, GC Tfh cells, and Tfh markers in PDK1-deficient mice.

claim: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells exhibit severe defects in migratory response toward CXCL13
source: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells exhibited severe defects in migratory response toward CXCL13 (Figure 1G), indicating impairment of the follicular migratory potential of Tfh cells in the absence of PDK1 may constrain GC responses.
evidence: The claim is supported by chemotaxis transwell assay data shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Impairment of the follicular migratory potential of Tfh cells in the absence of PDK1 may constrain GC responses
source: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells exhibited severe defects in migratory response toward CXCL13 (Figure 1G), indicating impairment of the follicular migratory potential of Tfh cells in the absence of PDK1 may constrain GC responses.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed migration defect and its potential consequences.

claim: GC B cells are profoundly impaired in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared with WT mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed GC B cells and plasma cells were profoundly impaired in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared with WT mice (Figure 1H,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1H,I.

claim: Plasma cells are profoundly impaired in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared with WT mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Flow cytometry analysis revealed GC B cells and plasma cells were profoundly impaired in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice compared with WT mice (Figure 1H,I).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1H,I.

claim: PNA+ GC areas in spleens of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice are smaller than those in WT littermates on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: In concert with decreased GC B cells, PNA+ GCs areas in spleens of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice were also smaller than those in WT littermates (Figure 1J).
evidence: The claim is supported by confocal microscopy analysis shown in Figure 1J.

claim: The concentrations of LCMV-specific IgG in the serum of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice are much lower than WT mice on 8 dpi and 56 dpi
source: Correspondingly, the concentrations of LCMV-specific IgG in the serum of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice were much lower than WT mice on 8 dpi and 56 dpi (Figure 1K).
evidence: The claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 1K.

claim: PDK1 plays an indispensable role in Tfh and GC B-cell differentiation as well as antibody production
source: These data corroborated an indispensable role of PDK1 in Tfh and GC B-cell differentiation as well as antibody production.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental observations including reduced Tfh cells, GC B cells, plasma cells, and LCMV-specific IgG in PDK1-deficient mice.

claim: Loss of PDK1 leads to significant reduction of Tfh cells upon KLH immunization on day 8
source: Consistent with the results shown above, loss of PDK1 led to significant reduction of Tfh cells as well as impaired expression of Tfh markers on day 8 post-KLH immunization (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: Loss of PDK1 leads to impaired expression of Tfh markers on day 8 post-KLH immunization
source: Consistent with the results shown above, loss of PDK1 led to significant reduction of Tfh cells as well as impaired expression of Tfh markers on day 8 post-KLH immunization (Figure 2A–D).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2A-D.

claim: Both GC B cells and plasma cells are decreased in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice on day 8 post-KLH immunization
source: Besides, both GC B cells and plasma cells were decreased in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice (Figure 2E,F).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2E,F.

claim: PDK1 positively regulates Tfh cell differentiation and effector functions upon different antigens challenge
source: These data collectively demonstrated that PDK1 positively regulates Tfh cell differentiation and effector functions upon different antigens challenge.
evidence: The claim is inferred from consistent observations across both LCMV infection and KLH immunization models.

claim: CD4+ T cells from Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice show greater expression of IFNγ, IL-4, and IL-17a than those in WT mice upon KLH immunization
source: CD4+ T cells from Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice showed greater expression of IFNγ, IL-4, and IL-17a than those in WT mice (Figure 2—figure supplement 1), which is consistent with previous report (Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1 and is consistent with a previous citation.

claim: PDK1 may also involve in other T helper cell differentiation under immunized condition
source: These results indicated that PDK1 may also involve in other T helper cell differentiation under immunized condition.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on the observed increased expression of cytokines associated with other T helper cell subsets.

claim: CD45.2+ cells from Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice account for less than 1% of the total Tfh cells and GC Tfh cells in bone marrow chimeras on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: We found CD45.2+ cells from Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice only accounted for less than 1% of the total Tfh cells and GC Tfh cells, while CD45.2+ cells of WT origin contributed to 23.1–29.7% among Tfh and GC Tfh cells (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of bone marrow chimeras shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: CD45.2+ cells of WT origin contribute to 23.1–29.7% among Tfh and GC Tfh cells in bone marrow chimeras on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: We found CD45.2+ cells from Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre mice only accounted for less than 1% of the total Tfh cells and GC Tfh cells, while CD45.2+ cells of WT origin contributed to 23.1–29.7% among Tfh and GC Tfh cells (Figure 3C–E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry analysis of bone marrow chimeras shown in Figure 3C-E.

claim: The expression levels of PD-1, ICOS, and Bcl-6 are substantially reduced in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells compared with WT cells in bone marrow chimeras
source: Additionally, the expression levels of PD-1, ICOS, and Bcl-6 were substantially reduced in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells compared with WT cells (Figure 3F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from bone marrow chimeras shown in Figure 3F,G.

claim: PDK1 has an intrinsic role in regulating Tfh cell differentiation
source: Collectively, these data thus confirmed the intrinsic role of PDK1 in regulating Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from bone marrow chimera experiments showing cell-intrinsic defects in PDK1-deficient cells.

claim: Both the frequency and cell numbers of Bcl-6+CXCR5+ Tfh cells of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER::SMARTA mice are remarkably decreased compared with WT counterparts on 3 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: On 3 dpi, both the frequency and cell numbers of Bcl-6+CXCR5+ Tfh cells of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER::SMARTA mice were remarkably decreased compared with those of WT counterparts (Figure 4C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4C.

claim: Both PDK1-deficient activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+ Tfh cells exhibit slower proliferation on 3 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Moreover, both PDK1-deficient activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+ Tfh cells exhibited slower proliferation (Figure 4D), while the apoptosis was not altered in these cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Apoptosis is not altered in PDK1-deficient activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+ Tfh cells on 3 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Moreover, both PDK1-deficient activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+ Tfh cells exhibited slower proliferation (Figure 4D), while the apoptosis was not altered in these cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by Caspase-3 staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: The expression of Tfh cell-related genes Tcf7, Cxcr5, Bcl6, and Pdcd1 is remarkably decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells on 3 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: We further sorted CXCR5+ Tfh cells and performed quantitative RT-PCR analysis. The expression of Tfh cell-related genes Tcf7, Cxcr5, Bcl6, and Pdcd1 was remarkably decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells (Figure 4E).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: PDK1 is essential for proliferation and commitment of early Tfh cells
source: These results suggested that PDK1 is essential for proliferation and commitment of early Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations of reduced Tfh cell numbers, slower proliferation, and decreased expression of Tfh-related genes in PDK1-deficient cells at early time points.

claim: Tfh cells and GC Tfh cells are decreased in tamoxifen-treated Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER mice on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong when PDK1 is deleted from day 4 to day 7 post-infection
source: On 8 dpi, we observed decreased Tfh cells and GC Tfh cells in tamoxifen-treated Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER mice (Figure 4H).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 4H.

claim: Both activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+CD44+ Tfh cells show slower proliferation in the absence of PDK1 on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong when PDK1 is deleted from day 4 to day 7 post-infection
source: Moreover, both activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+CD44+ Tfh cells showed slower proliferation in the absence of PDK1 (Figure 4I).
evidence: The claim is supported by BrdU incorporation assay data shown in Figure 4I.

claim: Apoptosis of activated CD4+ T cells and CXCR5+CD44+ Tfh cells is not affected by PDK1 deficiency on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong when PDK1 is deleted from day 4 to day 7 post-infection
source: While the apoptosis of these two subsets was not affected (Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by Caspase-3 staining data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: PDK1 is required for expansion and maintenance of late Tfh cell
source: These results indicated that PDK1 is also required for expansion and maintenance of late Tfh cell.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations of reduced Tfh cells and slower proliferation when PDK1 is deleted at later stages of differentiation.

claim: 1238 genes are upregulated and 354 genes are downregulated in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared to WT Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: One thousand two hundred and thirty-eight upregulated and 354 downregulated genes in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells were identified by RNA-seq analysis (Figure 5A).
evidence: The claim is supported by RNA-seq analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: A dysregulation of diverse pathways is observed in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells, in particular PI3K-AKT signaling pathway
source: Moreover, a dysregulation of diverse pathways was observed, in particular PI3K-AKT signaling pathway (Figure 5B).
evidence: The claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Tfh signature genes are negatively enriched in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells
source: Then, we selected a Tfh gene set (Choi et al., 2015) for gene set enrichment analysis (GSEA). The Tfh signature genes were negatively enriched in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells (Figure 5C).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5C using a Tfh gene set from a previous study.

claim: The expression of Tfh cell-related genes Cxcr5, Bcl6, Tcf7, and Icos is decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared with WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: We found the expression of Tfh cell-related genes Cxcr5, Bcl6, Tcf7, and Icos was decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared with those of WT cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: The expression of Maf is decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared with WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: The expression of Maf, which encodes transcription factor c-Maf, inducing IL-21 expression in Tfh cells to support GC response (Bauquet et al., 2009), was decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared with WT cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D and references the function of c-Maf from a previous study.

claim: c-Maf induces IL-21 expression in Tfh cells to support GC response
source: The expression of Maf, which encodes transcription factor c-Maf, inducing IL-21 expression in Tfh cells to support GC response (Bauquet et al., 2009), was decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells compared with WT cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Bauquet et al., 2009.

claim: The expression of Hif1a is substantially lower in PDK1-null Tfh cells compared with WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Moreover, the expression of Hif1a, which supports Tfh cell formation (Cho et al., 2019; He et al., 2019), was substantially lower in PDK1-null Tfh cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D and references the function of Hif1a from previous studies.

claim: Hif1a supports Tfh cell formation
source: Moreover, the expression of Hif1a, which supports Tfh cell formation (Cho et al., 2019; He et al., 2019), was substantially lower in PDK1-null Tfh cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2019 and He et al., 2019.

claim: Expression of Gzmb, Id2, Gata3, and Prdm1 is higher in PDK1-null Tfh cells than in WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Whereas expression of other effector cells-relevant genes Gzmb (which encodes granzyme B), Id2, Gata3, and Prdm1 was higher in PDK1-null Tfh cells than those in WT cells (Figure 5D).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative RT-PCR data shown in Figure 5D.

claim: PDK1 is indispensable for maintaining Tfh cell identity
source: Taken together, these data strongly suggested that PDK1 is indispensable for maintaining Tfh cell identity.
evidence: The claim is inferred from RNA-seq and RT-PCR data showing altered expression of Tfh-related genes and increased expression of other effector cell genes in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells show reduced expression of signatures in the gene set 'Up-regulated under anti-CD28'
source: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells showed reduced expression of signatures in the gene set 'Up-regulated under anti-CD28' containing up-regulated genes upon anti-CD28 stimulation (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells show increased expression of signatures in the gene set 'Down-regulated under anti-ICOS-L'
source: Moreover, Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells showed increased expression of signatures in the gene set 'Down-regulated under anti-ICOS-L' containing down-regulated genes upon ICOS-L blocking (Figure 5E).
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 5E.

claim: CD28- or ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity may involve in Tfh cell differentiation
source: These analyses suggested that CD28- or ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity may involve in Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on GSEA results showing enrichment of CD28- and ICOS-related gene signatures.

claim: Anti-ICOS only can elicit higher level of p-AKTT308 in CD4+ T cells
source: The results indicated that anti-ICOS only could elicit higher level of p-AKTT308, and combination of anti-ICOS plus anti-CD3e or/and anti-CD28 had a similar effect with anti-ICOS only (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: Combination of anti-ICOS plus anti-CD3e or/and anti-CD28 has a similar effect on p-AKTT308 level as anti-ICOS only in CD4+ T cells
source: The results indicated that anti-ICOS only could elicit higher level of p-AKTT308, and combination of anti-ICOS plus anti-CD3e or/and anti-CD28 had a similar effect with anti-ICOS only (Figure 5F,G).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 5F,G.

claim: ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity is essential for Tfh cells
source: These results further strengthen the notion that ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity is essential for Tfh cells, which is corresponding to the previous report that ICOS-driven PI3K signaling is indispensable for Tfh cell differentiation (Gigoux et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the p-AKT stimulation data and is consistent with a previous citation.

claim: ICOS-driven PI3K signaling is indispensable for Tfh cell differentiation
source: These results further strengthen the notion that ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity is essential for Tfh cells, which is corresponding to the previous report that ICOS-driven PI3K signaling is indispensable for Tfh cell differentiation (Gigoux et al., 2009).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Gigoux et al., 2009.

claim: Both Raptor and Rictor-activated genes are significantly enriched in WT Tfh cells
source: We observed both Raptor and Rictor-activated genes were significantly enriched in WT Tfh cells, while Raptor and Rictor-suppressed genes were remarkably enriched in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Raptor and Rictor-suppressed genes are remarkably enriched in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells
source: We observed both Raptor and Rictor-activated genes were significantly enriched in WT Tfh cells, while Raptor and Rictor-suppressed genes were remarkably enriched in Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: PDK1 and mTORC1/mTORC2 regulate a common subset of target genes in Tfh cells
source: These results indicated that PDK1 and mTORC1/mTORC2 regulate a common subset of target genes in the Tfh cells (Figure 6A).
evidence: The claim is inferred from GSEA showing enrichment of Raptor and Rictor-regulated genes in WT versus PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells show decreased amounts of both basal and phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 compared with WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: We found Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells showed decreased amounts of both basal and phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 compared with WT cells (Figure 6B), which were consistent with previous observations in B cells (Venigalla et al., 2013), suggesting phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 was interdependent in Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6B and is consistent with a previous citation.

claim: Phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 is interdependent in Tfh cells
source: We found Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre Tfh cells showed decreased amounts of both basal and phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 compared with WT cells (Figure 6B), which were consistent with previous observations in B cells (Venigalla et al., 2013), suggesting phosphorylation of AKT at T308 and S473 was interdependent in Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that both T308 and S473 phosphorylation are reduced in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: The phosphorylation level of PKCζ/λ is comparable between PDK1-deficient and WT Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: However, the phosphorylation level of PKCζ/λ, another target of PDK1, was comparable between PDK1-deficient and WT Tfh cells (Figure 6—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Both basal and phosphorylation levels of FoxO1/3a are substantially reduced in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: AKT phosphorylates FoxOs, and we observed both basal and phosphorylation levels of FoxO1/3a were substantially reduced in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C and references the known relationship between AKT and FoxOs.

claim: FoxO1 is excluded as a potential downstream target of PDK1 in Tfh cells due to its repression role in Tfh cell differentiation
source: Based on these observations, we excluded FoxO1 as a potential downstream target due to its repression role in Tfh cell differentiation (Stone et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that FoxO1 is reduced in PDK1-deficient cells, which would be expected to promote rather than inhibit Tfh differentiation, and is supported by a citation.

claim: FoxO1 has a repression role in Tfh cell differentiation
source: Based on these observations, we excluded FoxO1 as a potential downstream target due to its repression role in Tfh cell differentiation (Stone et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Stone et al., 2015.

claim: mTORC1 activity is significantly decreased with the ablation of PDK1 in Tfh cells, as indicated by impaired S6 phosphorylation and reduced Hif1α expression
source: AKT also activates mTORC1, a positive regulator for Tfh cell development (Zeng et al., 2016), and in line with the loss of AKT activation, mTORC1 activity was significantly decreased with the ablation of PDK1, as indicated by impaired S6 phosphorylation and reduced Hif1α expression (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C and references the known relationship between AKT and mTORC1, as well as a citation.

claim: mTORC1 is a positive regulator for Tfh cell development
source: AKT also activates mTORC1, a positive regulator for Tfh cell development (Zeng et al., 2016), and in line with the loss of AKT activation, mTORC1 activity was significantly decreased with the ablation of PDK1, as indicated by impaired S6 phosphorylation and reduced Hif1α expression (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zeng et al., 2016.

claim: PDK1-dependent AKT activation is essential for Tfh cell commitment
source: Taken together, we concluded PDK1-dependent AKT activation is essential for Tfh cell commitment.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations showing impaired AKT phosphorylation and downstream signaling in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: Phosphorylation of GSK3β is remarkably reduced in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Consistent with decreased p-AKT, phosphorylation of GSK3β was remarkably reduced in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Expression level of TCF1 is much lower in PDK1-null Tfh cells than in WT cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Moreover, expression level of TCF1 was much lower in PDK1-null Tfh cells than that of WT cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: Decreased GSK3β phosphorylation in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells causes enhanced GSK3β activity
source: Decreased GSK3β phosphorylation in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells caused enhanced GSK3β activity (Figure 6C), which was accounted for impaired TCF1 level.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the known relationship between GSK3β phosphorylation and its activity.

claim: Enhanced GSK3β activity in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells accounts for impaired TCF1 level
source: Decreased GSK3β phosphorylation in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells caused enhanced GSK3β activity (Figure 6C), which was accounted for impaired TCF1 level.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the known relationship between GSK3β activity and TCF1 stability.

claim: mTORC1-mediated STAT3 phosphorylation induces TCF1 expression in follicular regulatory helper (Tfr) cells
source: It has recently reported that mTORC1-mediated STAT3 phosphorylation induced TCF1 expression in follicular regulatory helper (Tfr) cells (Xu et al., 2017).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2017.

claim: Decreased phosphorylation of STAT3 at Ser727 is observed in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Similarly, we also observed decreased phosphorylation of STAT3 at Ser727 in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells (Figure 6C).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6C.

claim: PDK1 may promote Tfh cell differentiation via both mTORC1- and mTORC2-dependent expression of TCF1
source: These analyses collectively suggested that PDK1 may promote Tfh cell differentiation via both mTORC1- and mTORC2-dependent expression of TCF1.
evidence: The claim is speculative, based on observations of decreased p-GSK3β (mTORC2-related) and p-STAT3 (mTORC1-related) in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: TCF1 overexpression promotes differentiation of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER::SMARTA CD4+ T cells into Tfh cells
source: On 8 dpi, EV-infected Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER::SMARTA CD4+ T cells remained defects in the generation of Tfh cells compared with WT cells, while TCF1 retrovirus promoted differentiation of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER::SMARTA CD4+ T cells into Tfh cells (Figure 6D, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from retroviral transduction experiments shown in Figure 6D and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: The cell numbers of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER Tfh cells are partially rectified by TCF1 overexpression
source: In addition, the cell numbers of Pdk1fl/fl::Rosa26CreER Tfh cells were partially rectified by TCF1 (Figure 6E).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data shown in Figure 6E.

claim: Overexpression of a constitutive active form of STAT3 (STAT3-CA) can rectify the defective Tfh cells in the absence of PDK1
source: Moreover, overexpression of a constitutive active form of STAT3 (STAT3-CA) could also rectify the defective Tfh cells in the absence of PDK1 (Figure 6D,E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from retroviral transduction experiments shown in Figure 6D,E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Forced expression of Bcl-6 can partially restore the defective Tfh cell differentiation of PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells
source: Besides, we also found forced expression of Bcl-6 or CXCR5 could partially restore the defective Tfh cell differentiation of PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells (Figure 6D,E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from retroviral transduction experiments shown in Figure 6D,E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Forced expression of CXCR5 can partially restore the defective Tfh cell differentiation of PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells
source: Besides, we also found forced expression of Bcl-6 or CXCR5 could partially restore the defective Tfh cell differentiation of PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells (Figure 6D,E, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by flow cytometry data from retroviral transduction experiments shown in Figure 6D,E and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B.

claim: TCF1 serves as one of critical regulators downstream of PDK1 in promoting Tfh cell differentiation
source: Collectively, our data demonstrated that TCF1 serves as one of critical regulators downstream of PDK1 in promoting Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from rescue experiments showing that TCF1 overexpression can partially restore Tfh cell differentiation in PDK1-deficient cells.

claim: The generation of Tfh cells is severely compromised in PDK1-deficient mice upon acute LCMV infection and KLH immunization
source: The generation of Tfh cells was severely compromised in PDK1-deficient mice upon acute LCMV infection and KLH immunization.
evidence: The claim summarizes findings from multiple experiments described in the Results section.

claim: GC responses are impaired as a consequence of defective Tfh cells in PDK1-deficient mice
source: Correspondingly, the GC responses were also impaired as a consequence of defective Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations of reduced GC B cells, plasma cells, and antibody production in PDK1-deficient mice.

claim: PDK1 controls Tfh cells in a cell-intrinsic fashion
source: BM chimera results further revealed PDK1 controls Tfh cells in a cell-intrinsic fashion.
evidence: The claim is supported by bone marrow chimera experiments showing competitive disadvantage of PDK1-deficient cells.

claim: PDK1 is essential for both early expansion and late maintenance of Tfh cells

claim: PDK1 is critical for the development and B-cell helper function of Tfh cells

evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple experimental observations throughout the study.

claim: CD28 and ICOS are two key costimulatory receptors expressed by Tfh cells, both of which activate PI3Kδ and are essential for Tfh cell differentiation
source: CD28 and ICOS are two key costimulatory receptors expressed by Tfh cells, both of which activate PI3Kδ and are essential for Tfh cell differentiation (Preite et al., 2018b).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Preite et al., 2018b.

claim: ICOS-dependent PI3K signal exerts nonredundant function in the generation of Tfh cells

claim: ICOS functions as upstream activator of PDK1 in CD4+ T cells

evidence: The claim is supported by GSEA and flow cytometry data showing ICOS stimulation increases p-AKT levels.

claim: Tfh cells exhibit higher expression of PDK1 than Th1 cells and naïve CD4+ T cells

claim: ICOS-dependent PDK1 activity is pivotal for Tfh cells

claim: PI3K is a critical component of pathway driving Tfh cell differentiation and GC formation
source: It is well elaborated that PI3K is a critical component of pathway driving Tfh cell differentiation and GC formation supported by data from PI3K-targeting mice as well as mice and humans expressing activating mutants (Rolf et al., 2010; Preite et al., 2018a; Preite et al., 2018b; Lucas et al., 2014).

claim: Activation of PI3K facilitates the recruitment of PDK1 and AKT to the plasma membrane through their PH domains
source: Activation of PI3K facilitates the recruitment of PDK1 and AKT to the plasma membrane through their PH domains, which enables phosphorylation of T308 within the catalytic domain of AKT.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about PI3K-PDK1-AKT signaling.

claim: For AKT to be fully activated, a second crucial residue (S473) located in a hydrophobic motif within AKT's regulatory domain must be phosphorylated by protein kinases like mTORC2
source: To be fully activated, a second crucial residue (S473) located in a hydrophobic motif within AKT's regulatory domain must be phosphorylated by protein kinases like mTORC2 (Fayard et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Fayard et al., 2010 and represents established knowledge.

claim: mTORC2-deficient mice exhibit severely impaired Tfh cells by activating Tfh cell repressor FoxO1 expression
source: mTORC2-deficient mice exhibited severely impaired Tfh cells by activating Tfh cell repressor FoxO1 expression (Zeng et al., 2016; Hao et al., 2018), and we observed the phenotypes of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre cells almost recapitulated the defects of mTORC2-deficient Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Zeng et al., 2016 and Hao et al., 2018.

claim: The phenotypes of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre cells almost recapitulate the defects of mTORC2-deficient Tfh cells
source: mTORC2-deficient mice exhibited severely impaired Tfh cells by activating Tfh cell repressor FoxO1 expression (Zeng et al., 2016; Hao et al., 2018), and we observed the phenotypes of Pdk1fl/fl::Cd4-Cre cells almost recapitulated the defects of mTORC2-deficient Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is inferred from comparison of PDK1-deficient and mTORC2-deficient phenotypes.

claim: mTORC2-deficient T cells exhibit decreased phosphorylation of p-AKT at Ser473
source: mTORC2-deficient T cells exhibited decreased phosphorylation of p-AKT at Ser473 (Zeng et al., 2016), whereas, in our experimental system, we found a reduction of both phosphorylated T308 and S473 levels in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells, similar phenomena were also observed in PDK1-null B cells (Venigalla et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zeng et al., 2016.

claim: PDK1-AKT-FoxOs signaling may not be responsible for defective Tfh cells in PDK1-null mice
source: These results suggested that PDK1-AKT-FoxOs signaling may not be responsible for defective Tfh cells in PDK1-null mice, as FoxO1 is a negative regulator for Tfh cell formation (Stone et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is inferred from the observation that FoxO1 is reduced in PDK1-deficient cells, which would not explain the Tfh defect, and is supported by a citation.

claim: Compromised mTORC1 activity attenuates protein synthesis and cell proliferation, which are essential for Tfh cell differentiation
source: Compromised mTORC1 activity in turn attenuates protein synthesis and cell proliferation, which are essential for Tfh cell differentiation (Zeng et al., 2016).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Zeng et al., 2016 and represents established knowledge.

claim: Loss of Hif1α in CD4+ T cells impairs Tfh cell differentiation
source: Meanwhile, we found the expression of both Hif1a mRNA and Hif1α protein was significantly decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells, which may also contribute to the defective phenotype as loss of Hif1α in CD4+ T cells impairs Tfh cell differentiation (Cho et al., 2019; He et al., 2019).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Cho et al., 2019 and He et al., 2019.

claim: PDK1-dependent downstream molecular pathways are indispensable for Tfh cell biology
source: These results collectively indicated that PDK1-dependent downstream molecular pathways are indispensable for Tfh cell biology.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations of impaired downstream signaling in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: TCF1 is expressed at an extremely high level in Tfh cells post-viral infection
source: Transcription factor TCF1 is expressed at an extremely high level in Tfh cells post-viral infection and exerts crucial roles in generation, maintenance, and effector functions of Tfh cells by repressing Prdm1 and Il2ra and promoting Bcl6 expression (Shao et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2015; Choi et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: TCF1 exerts crucial roles in generation, maintenance, and effector functions of Tfh cells by repressing Prdm1 and Il2ra and promoting Bcl6 expression
source: Transcription factor TCF1 is expressed at an extremely high level in Tfh cells post-viral infection and exerts crucial roles in generation, maintenance, and effector functions of Tfh cells by repressing Prdm1 and Il2ra and promoting Bcl6 expression (Shao et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2015; Choi et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: β-catenin is a coactivator of TCF1 that is negatively regulated by p-GSK3β
source: It has been proposed that β-catenin, a coactivator of TCF1 that is negatively regulated by p-GSK3β, linking PI3K-AKT and TCF1 (Yang et al., 2016; Zhou et al., 2010).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Yang et al., 2016 and Zhou et al., 2010.

claim: mTORC1 controls TCF1 expression in Tfr cells by phosphorylated STAT3
source: Besides, it has been reported that mTORC1 controls TCF1 expression in Tfr cells by phosphorylated STAT3 (Xu et al., 2017 ).
evidence: The claim is supported by a citation to Xu et al., 2017.

claim: Both the p-GSK3βS9 and p-STAT3S727 levels are significantly decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Correspondingly, we found both the p-GSK3βS9 and p-STAT3S727 levels were significantly decreased in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: PDK1-null Tfh cells show both impaired Tcf7 mRNA and TCF1 protein level on 8 dpi with LCMV Armstrong
source: Furthermore, PDK1-null Tfh cells showed both impaired Tcf7 mRNA and TCF1 protein level.

claim: Reconstituting PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells with TCF1 rectifies their defects in the generation of Tfh cells
source: Reconstituting PDK1-deficient CD4+ T cells with TCF1 rectifies their defects in the generation of Tfh cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by retroviral transduction experiments shown in Figure 6D,E.

claim: PDK1-dependent TCF1 expression contributes to Tfh cell formation
source: These observations collectively suggested that PDK1-dependent TCF1 expression contributes to Tfh cell formation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations including reduced TCF1 in PDK1-deficient cells and rescue by TCF1 overexpression.

claim: PDK1 activates AKT in Tfh cells via phosphorylating both Thr308 and Ser473 residues
source: Our data further suggested PDK1 activates AKT in Tfh cells via phosphorylating both Thr308 and Ser473 residues.
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations of reduced phosphorylation at both sites in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: p-AKT activates mTORC1, and mTORC1 subsequently drives protein synthesis and Hif1α expression and supports TCF1 expression by p-STAT3 to sustain Tfh cell differentiation
source: On the one side, p-AKT in turn activates mTORC1, and mTORC1 subsequently drives protein synthesis and Hif1α expression and supports TCF1 expression by p-STAT3 to sustain Tfh cell differentiation.
evidence: The claim is inferred from multiple observations of impaired mTORC1 signaling, reduced Hif1α, reduced p-STAT3, and reduced TCF1 in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: p-AKT suppresses GSK3β activity and ultimately promotes TCF1 expression
source: On the other side, p-AKT also suppresses GSK3β activity and ultimately promotes TCF1 expression (Figure 7).
evidence: The claim is inferred from observations of reduced p-GSK3β and reduced TCF1 in PDK1-deficient Tfh cells.

claim: PDK1 is a critical regulator for Tfh cell development for both early expansion and late maintenance by mainly modulating TCF1 expression
source: Therefore, our study uncovers PDK1 as a critical regulator for Tfh cell development for both early expansion and late maintenance by mainly modulating TCF1 expression.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the entire body of experimental evidence presented in the study.

claim: PDK1 is a crucial regulator for immune cell development by connecting PI3K to downstream AKT signaling
source: The kinase PDK1 is a crucial regulator for immune cell development by connecting PI3K to downstream AKT signaling.
evidence: The claim is based on established scientific knowledge about PDK1 function.

claim: PDK1 is crucial for multiple types of immune cell development, such as hematopoietic stem cells, B cells, NK cells, T cells, and cytolytic CD8+ cells
source: PDK1 is crucial for multiple types of immune cell development, such as hematopoietic stem cells, B cells, NK cells, T cells, and cytolytic CD8+ cells (Park et al., 2009; Baracho et al., 2014; Venigalla et al., 2013; Yang et al., 2015; Finlay et al., 2012).

source: Tfh cells are a specialized population that provides cognate help in germinal center (GC) to facilitate immunoglobulin affinity maturation and heavy-chain class switching, and ultimately promote generation of high-affinity antibodies of diverse isotypes, long-lived plasma cells, and memory B cells (Crotty, 2014).

source: Tfh cells are a specialized population that provides cognate help in germinal center (GC) to facilitate immunoglobulin affinity maturation and heavy-chain class switching, and ultimately promote generation of high-affinity antibodies of diverse isotypes, long-lived plasma cells, and memory B cells (Crotty, 2014).

claim: The characteristic features of Tfh cells are defined as expression of CXCR5, ICOS, PD-1, Bcl-6, and IL-21

source: Differentiation of Tfh cell relies on precisely orchestrated transcriptional program, which lies in the mutually antagonistic Bcl-6-Blimp1 as the core regulatory axis.

source: Bcl-6 is indispensable for the divergence of CD4+ T cells into Tfh lineage, whereas Blimp1 programs Th1 cell formation (Johnston et al., 2009; Yu et al., 2009; Nurieva et al., 2009).

claim: Blimp1 programs Th1 cell formation

evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: TCF1 supports Tfh cell specification by promoting Bcl-6 and repressing Blimp1 expression
source: TCF1 (encoded by Tcf7) supports Tfh cell specification by promoting Bcl-6 and repressing Blimp1 expression, revealing a key role of TCF1 in the regulation of the Bcl-6-Blimp1 axis (Shao et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2015; Choi et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).

claim: TCF1 plays a key role in the regulation of the Bcl-6-Blimp1 axis
source: TCF1 (encoded by Tcf7) supports Tfh cell specification by promoting Bcl-6 and repressing Blimp1 expression, revealing a key role of TCF1 in the regulation of the Bcl-6-Blimp1 axis (Shao et al., 2019; Wu et al., 2015; Choi et al., 2015; Xu et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: The differentiation of Tfh is more dependent on signals provided by both TCR and co-receptors compared with other T helper cells
source: Compared with other T helper cells, the differentiation of Tfh is more dependent on signals provided by both TCR and co-receptors (Deenick et al., 2010; Baumjohann et al., 2013).

source: The PI3K signaling via AKT is responsible for transduction of Tfh cell-dependent TCR signals and ICOS co-stimulation and essential for Tfh cell differentiation.

source: Previous studies have revealed inactivation of PI3K catalytic subunit p110δ or regulatory subunit p85α almost completely abolishes Tfh cell differentiation (Rolf et al., 2010; Leavenworth et al., 2015), whereas mice that express the E1020K activating mutant of p110δ or have a T cell-specific deficiency of PTEN exhibit enhanced Tfh cell formation (Preite et al., 2018a; Shrestha et al., 2015).

source: Previous studies have revealed inactivation of PI3K catalytic subunit p110δ or regulatory subunit p85α almost completely abolishes Tfh cell differentiation (Rolf et al., 2010; Leavenworth et al., 2015), whereas mice that express the E1020K activating mutant of p110δ or have a T cell-specific deficiency of PTEN exhibit enhanced Tfh cell formation (Preite et al., 2018a; Shrestha et al., 2015).
evidence: The claim is supported by citations to Preite et al., 2018a and Shrestha et al., 2015.
